claims.quote: Loss-of-function mutations in CDKL5 are associated with a severe neurodevelopmental encephalopathy.
Loss-of-function mutations in CDKL5 are associated with a severe neurodevelopmental encephalopathy.
Here, we identified cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5), known to function in neurodevelopment, as an essential regulator of virophagy.
deletion of CDKL5 or expression of a clinically relevant pathogenic mutant of CDKL5 reduced virophagy of Sindbis virus (SINV)

claims.object_text: intracellular SINV capsid protein aggregates and cellular cytotoxicity
claims.quote: increased intracellular accumulation of SINV capsid protein aggregates and cellular cytotoxicity
Cdkl5-knockout mice displayed increased viral antigen accumulation and neuronal cell death after SINV infection and enhanced lethality after infection with several neurotropic viruses.

CDKL5 directly binds the canonical selective autophagy receptor p62
CDKL5 directly binds the canonical selective autophagy receptor p62 and phosphorylates p62 at T269/S272 to promote its interaction with viral capsid aggregates.

claims.object_text: formation of large p62 inclusion bodies that capture viral capsids
claims.quote: CDKL5-mediated phosphorylation of p62 facilitated the formation of large p62 inclusion bodies that captured viral capsids to initiate capsid targeting to autophagic machinery.
